--- title: 2 - Setting up --- ::: {#3b2470b8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import mewpy mewpy.info() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` MEWpy version: 0.1.36 Author: Vitor Pereira (2019-) and CEB University of Minho (2019-2023) Contact: vpereira@ceb.uminho.pt Available LP solvers: gurobi glpk Default LP solver: gurobi Available ODE solvers: scipy Default ODE solver: scipy Optimization Problems: AbstractKOProblem AbstractOUProblem CofactorSwapProblem CommunityKOProblem ETFLGKOProblem ETFLGOUProblem GKOProblem GOUProblem GeckoKOProblem GeckoOUProblem KcatOptProblem KineticKOProblem KineticOUProblem MediumProblem OptORFProblem OptRamProblem RKOProblem ROUProblem Available EA engines: inspyred jmetal Default EA engine: jmetal Available EAs: GA NSGAII NSGAIII SA SPEA2 ``` ::: ::: We will create a synthetic microbial consortium with two *E. coli* mutants growing in minimal medium. In one of the mutants we will knockout the glucose transporter and in the other we will knockout the ammonium transporter. ::: {#8104fddc .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from cobra.io import read_sbml_model from mewpy import get_simulator wild= read_sbml_model('data/models/e_coli_core.xml.gz') wildtype = get_simulator(wild) solution = wildtype.simulate() print(solution) solution.find('EX') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Set parameter Username Set parameter LicenseID to value 2582980 Academic license - for non-commercial use only - expires 2025-11-13 objective: 0.8739215069684301 Status: OPTIMAL Method:FBA ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Now we create our two mutants (`glc_ko` and `nh4_ko`): ::: {#6eb408ca .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} glc_ko = wildtype.copy() glc_ko.id = 'glc_ko' glc_ko.set_reaction_bounds('GLCpts', 0, 0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Read LP format model from file /tmp/tmppt6kbip6.lp Reading time = 0.00 seconds : 72 rows, 190 columns, 720 nonzeros ``` ::: ::: ::: {#d7c4237f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} nh4_ko = wildtype.copy() nh4_ko.id = 'nh4_ko' nh4_ko.set_reaction_bounds('NH4t', 0, 0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Read LP format model from file /tmp/tmpxi5zovkf.lp Reading time = 0.00 seconds : 72 rows, 190 columns, 720 nonzeros ``` ::: ::: ### Comparing models Community models require that metabolites have the same identifiers across all models. We can verify that by computing the metabolites, reactions and uptakes overlaps between a list models. ::: {#7300305e .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} from mewpy.com import * mets, rxns, over = jaccard_similarity_matrices([glc_ko, nh4_ko]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Read LP format model from file /tmp/tmp9szrxy_3.lp Reading time = 0.00 seconds : 72 rows, 190 columns, 720 nonzeros Read LP format model from file /tmp/tmptuwaaa2r.lp Reading time = 0.00 seconds : 72 rows, 190 columns, 720 nonzeros Read LP format model from file /tmp/tmpne0i34wz.lp Reading time = 0.00 seconds : 72 rows, 190 columns, 720 nonzeros Read LP format model from file /tmp/tmp3pc8v533.lp Reading time = 0.00 seconds : 72 rows, 190 columns, 720 nonzeros Read LP format model from file /tmp/tmp7_u_qndi.lp Reading time = 0.00 seconds : 72 rows, 190 columns, 720 nonzeros Read LP format model from file /tmp/tmp25uahe3k.lp Reading time = 0.00 seconds : 72 rows, 190 columns, 720 nonzeros Read LP format model from file /tmp/tmpqval9wjo.lp Reading time = 0.00 seconds : 72 rows, 190 columns, 720 nonzeros Read LP format model from file /tmp/tmpy0u00csa.lp Reading time = 0.00 seconds : 72 rows, 190 columns, 720 nonzeros ``` ::: ::: ::: {#9613a20f .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} mets ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### Building communities Let's initiate the `CommunityModel` class to create microbial communities from a list of models of individual species: ::: {#09b30c9d .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} from mewpy.model import CommunityModel community1 = CommunityModel([glc_ko, nh4_ko],flavor='cobra') sim_com = community1.get_community_model() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Read LP format model from file /tmp/tmprgmndwa6.lp Reading time = 0.00 seconds : 72 rows, 190 columns, 720 nonzeros Read LP format model from file /tmp/tmpcavb5lco.lp Reading time = 0.00 seconds : 72 rows, 190 columns, 720 nonzeros ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Organism: 0%| | 0/2 [00:00 lb ub EX_ac_e 0.0 1000.0 EX_acald_e 0.0 1000.0 EX_akg_e 0.0 1000.0 EX_co2_e -1000.0 1000.0 EX_etoh_e 0.0 1000.0 EX_for_e 0.0 1000.0 EX_fru_e 0.0 1000.0 EX_fum_e 0.0 1000.0 EX_glc__D_e -10.0 1000.0 EX_gln__L_e 0.0 1000.0 EX_glu__L_e 0.0 1000.0 EX_h_e -1000.0 1000.0 EX_h2o_e -1000.0 1000.0 EX_lac__D_e 0.0 1000.0 EX_mal__L_e 0.0 1000.0 EX_nh4_e -1000.0 1000.0 EX_o2_e -1000.0 1000.0 EX_pi_e -1000.0 1000.0 EX_pyr_e 0.0 1000.0 EX_succ_e 0.0 1000.0 ``` ::: ::: ## 3 - Simulation using FBA A very simple way to simulate a microbial community is to merge the individual models into a single model that mimics a "super organism", where each microbe lives inside its own compartment, and run a (conventional) FBA simulation for this super organism. ::: {#e2956991 .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} sol_com = sim_com.simulate(constraints=M9) print(sol_com) sol_com.find('EX') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` objective: 0.40757209363986224 Status: OPTIMAL Method:FBA ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=12} ```{=html}
